description: The period from 1885 to 1905 in Indian History is characterized as the Moderate Phase. It witnessed the establishment of the Indian National Congress (INC) led by early nationalists who firmly believed in constitutional agitation, peaceful protests, and demanding gradual political reforms.

sections.title: Formation of the Indian National Congress
sections.description: The Indian National Congress was established in 1885 to provide a pan-India political platform for educated Indians to voice their political and economic demands.

historical_events.event: Formation of the Indian National Union
historical_events.significance: Established by Allan Octavian Hume (A.O. Hume), a retired British civil servant, which served as the precursor organization to the Congress.
Held at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Bombay, attended by 72 delegates from across India.

important_facts.fact: Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee (W.C. Bonnerjee) served as the first President of the Indian National Congress.
Lord Dufferin was the Viceroy of India at the time of the formation of the INC.

sections.title: Major Theories regarding INC Formation
sections.description: Various historical theories have been proposed to explain the actual motive behind A.O. Hume's initiative to form the Indian National Congress.

key_concepts.explanation: Propounded by Lala Lajpat Rai, this theory suggests that A.O. Hume created the Congress as a 'safe outlet' to release the growing political discontent among Indians and protect the British Empire from another massive revolt like 1857.

Proposed by Gopal Krishna Gokhale, it argues that early Indian nationalists intentionally used A.O. Hume as a 'lightning conductor' (shield) to avoid immediate suppression of their political organization by the British government.

sections.title: Key Leaders and Methodology of the Moderate Phase
sections.description: The Moderate leaders had immense faith in the British sense of justice and fair play, and they restricted their struggle strictly within the legal framework.

key_concepts.explanation: The core methodology of the Moderates centered around Prayer, Petition, and Protest to persuade the British government to introduce reforms.
The method of demanding political rights peacefully and lawfully without resorting to violence or mass uprising.

key_associations.associated_with: The Grand Old Man of India
key_associations.extra_info: He was the first Indian to be elected as a Member of the British Parliament (House of Commons).
Often referred to as the 'Uncrowned King of Bengal'; he founded the Indian Association in 1876.
Founded the society in 1905 and is famously known as the political guru of Mahatma Gandhi.

sections.title: Economic Critique of British Imperialism
sections.description: The most significant intellectual contribution of the Moderates was exposing the systematic economic exploitation of India by British rule.

key_concepts.explanation: A theory highlighting that a massive portion of India's national wealth was being unilaterally transferred to Britain in the form of salaries, pensions, and administrative costs, without any adequate economic return, leading to extreme poverty in India.

key_associations.item: Poverty and Un-British Rule in India
key_associations.extra_info: A seminal book that comprehensively detailed and statistically proved the 'Drain of Wealth' from India.
The first authoritative book on the economic history of India, severely criticizing British land revenue policies.

sections.title: Important Congress Sessions (1885-1905)
sections.description: The early annual sessions of the Congress laid the foundational demographic and leadership structure for the Indian national movement.

historical_events.significance: Marked the historic merger of Surendranath Banerjee's Indian National Association with the Indian National Congress.
Badruddin Tyabji presided over this session, becoming the first Muslim President of the INC.
George Yule became the first European to preside over an Indian National Congress session.
Presided over by G.K. Gokhale, the Congress officially supported the Swadeshi Movement to protest against the impending Partition of Bengal.

sections.title: Achievements and Legacy of the Moderates
sections.description: Though criticized later for their mild approach, the Moderates successfully sowed the seeds of modern nationalism and achieved notable early concessions.

polity_articles.provision: Increased the number of additional members in the imperial and provincial legislative councils.
polity_articles.details: This act was a direct outcome of the pressure and constitutional demands put forward by the early Congress.

important_facts.fact: The Moderates successfully popularized the concepts of democracy, civil liberties, and secular nationalism among the Indian masses.
Due to their persistent demands for Indianization of services, the Aitchison Commission on Public Services was set up in 1886.
